me.json._description: Finding your own name, what is in your stack, and what you are allowed to change.

me/._description: Long sections of aos/me.json (self_tools, self_llm, self_system, self_history, self_hook); read them through aos/me.json.

errors.json._description: How to read a failed call: the `error:` line, `warning:` lines, and exit codes.

errors/._description: Long sections of aos/errors.json (common); read them through aos/errors.json.

world.json._description: The mental model: daemon = hardware, stack = memory, workspace = external memory, definition = source code, kernel = gatekeeper.

definition.json._description: What each file in a definition folder does (interfaces.json, loop.json, tools.json, hooks.json, cli.json ...), and which ones you have your own copy of.

body.json._description: Two kinds of body, agent-fsm and eca (claude, codex): brain, tools, hooks, system text, history; how to tell which you are.

status.json._description: The daemon table, the phases an agent can be in, and what each phase means for you.

brain.json._description: How a brain request travels, what an endpoint pack is, and how priority works.

agents.json._description: Tools subagent, agents_ctl and agent_def: your own subagents, any agent on the daemon table, and new definitions.

agents/._description: Long sections of aos/agents.json (subagent); read them through aos/agents.json.

rules.json._description: What you must not do, and why. Read this before doing anything that changes the system.

knowledge.json._description: The knowledge base: how to look things up (knowledge_read), which one you may write, when and how to write (knowledge_write).

cli/._description: Use these shell commands to manage agents, tools and daemon procs.

mailbox.json._description: Letters between agents: tools mailbox_peek, mailbox_read, mailbox_send; when you must answer; checking regularly without filling your history.

clock.json._description: Timers: clock letters to your queue (clock_register), or an on_clock hook that adds nothing to your history; which one to choose.

tools_def.json._description: Making your own tools: tool tools_def (new from the Python skeleton, check) and the Python helper tool_spec.

tools/._description: One node per stock tool (read, ls, write, edit, trash, shell ...): when to use it and which tool instead, examples with real output, errors.

packs.json._description: Your tools come in packs (look, change, delete, shell, gadgets, events, self, subagent, def, mailbox, knowledge): one sentence per tool, and how a pack is turned off.
